Great Magician's Catacomb


Setting

Tka-Rik’s underground dwelling is the turning point between Zak’s local search and his journey across the allods. Here the magician asks him to find surviving Joons, receives his discoveries and finally helps reveal the truth about At-Zako. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Water for the lizards and the Great Magician

The Hermit needs the water diverted by the orcs restored. Zak raises their dam and blocks the diversion canal; in return the lizard locates the magician in a ravine in the Remote Mountains. This information joins the tunnel instructions from the Khadaganian report. Zak passes the ancient defences and reaches Tka Rik (Tka-Lithan Richti-Nik). Tka-Rik explains that his dragonet has watched Zak since his unusual arrival. Bound to Gipath by his duty as its Great Magician, he offers help with Zak’s memory in exchange for bringing him two surviving young Joons. The first journey will be to Ingos to find the girl. Zak must leave his Gipath companions behind. Tka-Rik supplies an amulet for the return journey, but warns that it will work only once the girl has been found; his dragonet will travel with Zak. [5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 2, 10, 11, 12]

The world beyond Gipath

Tka-Rik places Gipath’s isolation in a longer history. Before the Sundering it belonged to a continent; the Joon civilisation and later states have left successive layers of ruins. The Night of Troubles destroyed many of those later realms. Cania and Khadagan survived, but Tka-Rik distinguishes their societies: he regards Cania as comparatively free, while warning that Khadagan subordinates everyone to someone stronger. His account gives Zak a wider setting for the local ruins and conflicts. [13, 14]

Lu-a-Jalla beneath the mines

The former punishment cell is empty. Zak follows the trail deeper into the Forbidden Catacombs until he finds Lu-a-Jalla, who first mistakes him for another captor. She has escaped the mercenaries and found protection through the ancient treaty between Joons and Wormheads. She rejects the nickname Princess and explains that Diera imprisoned her out of jealousy over the governor. Zak falls in love with her, but she remains faithful to At-Zako, who drew the Joon Curse away from her. Zak promises to respect that bond. They return to Tka-Rik, and the next mission becomes the search for her missing beloved on Suslanger. [15, 16, 17, 18, 3]

Tka-Rik’s warning about Suslanger

Before Zak leaves for Suslanger, Tka-Rik describes the Khadaganian hierarchy, in which even a master is subject to someone above him. Emperor Neseb is himself a powerful magician. Suslanger is a provincial backwater, but that does not make it safe. The old Joon portal provides a route there; informants and imperial attention make open enquiries about the missing Joon dangerous. [14, 19]

At-Zako: the search turns back on itself

Tka-Rik initially expects Zak to bring the missing Joon with him. Lu-a-Jalla defends the exhausted traveller, and Zak insists that he will continue for her sake even if reunion with At-Zako means losing her. The amulet changes everything: Tka-Rik discovers that its destination was Gipath. Only Zak arrived there in that unusual way. The man he has been seeking is himself, hidden by the Khadaganian transformation spell. Restored as At-Zako, he reassures Tka-Rik and reunites with Lu-a-Jalla. The memories of their earlier flight explain why the return of his identity also brings back the danger of the Curse. If companions have come from Suslanger, Tka-Rik sends them back by a safe route beyond the imperial guards. Their departure does not mean that they have settled on Gipath. [20, 21, 4, 22, 23]

The battle with the Joon Curse

The hurried transformation that concealed At-Zako nearly destroyed his memory. Tka-Rik cannot safely repeat it, so hiding as Zak is no longer an answer. He offers another choice: flee again under his temporary protection, or confront the Curse on Gipath. At-Zako chooses to defend his life with Lu-a-Jalla. Tka-Rik supplies ancient Joon equipment and joins him in the catacombs for the final battle. Defeating the Curse completes the campaign. [24, 25, 26, 27]
